source_read: PMC HTML full text PMC7299220 (Circ Genom Precis Med 2020;13(3):e002814; a short research article), all sections, acknowledgments, sources of funding and disclosures. Figures 1-4 are images; their printed values (data sources and case counts, blood pressure and lipid betas, smoking-adjusted odds ratios, stroke-type estimates) were read enlarged on the PMC figure pages in my own tab. The two Data Supplement files (methods, Tables VIII-XIV) were not read.

claims.note: Numbers check: systolic 0.12 (0.05 to 0.20) and diastolic 0.15 (0.05 to 0.25) per SD of log drinks a week. 'In units the paper's figure does not make clear' is fair. Figure 2 labels them mm Hg, but beside HDL cholesterol at 0.39 'mmol/L' the values are implausible on those scales, and the main text does not explain. Precision: the blood-pressure data are UK Biobank only (up to 367 284 people; Figure 1), not consortium summary data, so 'European summary data' would read better as 'UK Biobank summary data'. The ADH1B variant alone also went with higher systolic and diastolic pressure (values only in the supplement).

anchors.locator: Figure 2; Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 1st paragraph; Figure 1
anchors.extracted: Overall instrument (up to 94 variants), random-effects IVW, per SD of log drinks/week: systolic 0.12 (0.05 to 0.20; P=0.001; n 346 656), diastolic 0.15 (0.05 to 0.25; P=0.003; n 367 284), labelled mm Hg; HDL 0.39 (0.25 to 0.53) labelled mmol/L; outcome data UK Biobank.

anchors.locator: Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 2nd paragraph; Discussion › Possible Mechanisms, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: The ADH1B rs1229984 instrument alone was also associated with higher systolic and diastolic pressure (Table IX, supplement); the authors present this as replicating earlier genetic blood-pressure findings.

claims.note: Numbers check: CAD 1.16 (1.00 to 1.36; P=0.052), smoking-adjusted 1.08 (0.91 to 1.27), never-smokers 1.39 (0.98 to 1.96), instrument and smoking initiation 1.24 (1.15 to 1.33), up to 94 variants. 'The ADH1B variant alone was associated with coronary artery disease' is supported by the text (P<0.05; values only in supplement Table XIII), and the authors raise possible pleiotropy through education for that variant (beta -0.15 years). Instrument strength: genome-wide-significant variants from 941 280 people; no F statistic in the main text. Other pathways: smoking initiation (strong), education (weak, P=0.05), multivariable adjustment for smoking liability, weighted median, MR-PRESSO and MR-Egger (results in supplement), consortium-only and UK Biobank-only estimates similar. Limits: UK Biobank sample overlap, and linear analysis only (no test of U or J shapes). 'European summary data' is approximately right: the paper says most participants were of European ancestry.

anchors.locator: Figure 3, coronary artery disease rows; Results › Associations With CVD, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: CAD (90 079 cases, 461 812 non-cases; CARDIoGRAMplusC4D and UK Biobank): IVW 1.16 (1.00 to 1.36; P=0.052); smoking-adjusted 1.08 (0.91 to 1.27; P=0.389); UK Biobank never-smokers 1.39 (0.98 to 1.96; P=0.064); similar with consortium-only and UK Biobank data.

anchors.locator: Results › Associations With Potential Mediators and Confounders, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Overall alcohol instrument associated with smoking initiation, OR 1.24 (1.15 to 1.33; P=9.5x10^-9), and weakly with education, beta -0.09 years (-0.17 to 0.00; P=0.05).

anchors.locator: Results › Associations With CVD, 3rd paragraph; Discussion › Comparison With Other Studies, 2nd paragraph
anchors.extracted: rs1229984 alone associated (P<0.05) with CAD (Table XIII, supplement); the authors note its alcohol-increasing allele goes with less education, which could act through horizontal pleiotropy.

anchors.locator: Figure 1; Discussion › Strengths and Limitations, 2nd and 3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Instruments: up to 94 genome-wide-significant variants from 941 280 European-descent people; no F statistic in the text. UK Biobank in discovery, exposure and most outcome datasets (possible bias); population stratification not excluded; U- or J-shapes not examinable.

claims.overstatement: Minor. 'In European-descent summary data': the main stroke and atrial fibrillation analyses used consortium data that the paper does not restrict to European descent (results were similar when restricted, Table XII, supplement). 'Mostly European-descent' is accurate.
claims.note: Numbers check: stroke 1.27 (1.12 to 1.45), smoking-adjusted 1.21 (1.05 to 1.40), ischaemic 1.26 (1.09 to 1.46), intracerebral haemorrhage 3.53 (1.70 to 7.32); in the magnitude, subarachnoid haemorrhage 2.47 (1.08 to 5.62, UK Biobank, 1084 cases), ADH1B alone 1.31 (1.05 to 1.65) and 11.5 (1.31 to 101.46). Recomputed case counts: 60 341 + 4602 = 64 943 ischaemic strokes; 1545 + 1064 = 2609 intracerebral haemorrhages, matching Figure 1. The intracerebral estimate rests on 2609 cases and is imprecise, as is the ADH1B-only estimate (interval 1.31 to 101).

anchors.locator: Figure 3, stroke rows; Results › Associations With CVD, 1st paragraph; Abstract (Results)
anchors.extracted: Stroke (76 814 cases, 812 384 non-cases; MEGASTROKE and UK Biobank): IVW 1.27 (1.12 to 1.45; P=2.87x10^-4); smoking-adjusted 1.21 (1.05 to 1.40; P=0.010); consistent across methods, with consortium-only and UK Biobank data, and in never-smokers.

anchors.locator: Results › Associations With CVD, 2nd paragraph; Figure 4
anchors.extracted: Ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.09 to 1.46; P=0.002; MEGASTROKE plus UK Biobank); intracerebral haemorrhage 3.53 (1.70 to 7.32; P=0.001; ISGC plus UK Biobank); UK Biobank subarachnoid 2.47 (1.08 to 5.62); MEGASTROKE subtypes 1.11 to 1.30, intervals including 1; similar when restricted to European descent.

rs1229984 alone: any stroke associated (P<0.05); ischaemic stroke 1.31 (1.05 to 1.65; P=0.018); intracerebral haemorrhage 11.5 (1.31 to 101.46; P=0.027). Excluding rs1229984 gave results similar to the full set.

anchors.locator: Discussion › Comparison With Other Studies, 1st paragraph; Discussion › Strengths and Limitations, 3rd paragraph
anchors.extracted: Authors say the Chinese stroke findings hold in European ancestry, more strongly for intracerebral haemorrhage; limitations: low precision for outcomes with few cases, possible population stratification, most but not all participants of European ancestry.

claims.note: Numbers check: peripheral artery disease 3.05 (1.92 to 4.85), adjusted 2.55 (1.49 to 4.35), 3415 cases; abdominal aortic aneurysm 2.60 (1.15 to 5.89), adjusted 2.29 (0.89 to 5.93), 1094 cases; AF 1.17 (1.00 to 1.37), adjusted 1.11 (0.93 to 1.32); heart failure 1.00 (0.68 to 1.47), adjusted 0.88 (0.57 to 1.37); VTE 1.04 (0.77 to 1.39), adjusted 1.05 (0.75 to 1.47); aortic valve stenosis 1.03 (0.56 to 1.90), adjusted 0.94 (0.46 to 1.91); ADH1B alone positive for PAD, AVS and AAA. One detail: the magnitude says pleiotropy was 'indicated by MR-Egger', but the main text only says directional pleiotropy was indicated for aortic valve stenosis, without naming the test (Table X, supplement). Overlap: heart failure, VTE, PAD, AVS and AAA outcome data are UK Biobank only (Figure 1), the same cohort Biddinger et al. used, so 'two studies whose outcome data overlap' is right. AF came from AFGen, not UK Biobank. 'No association was found' for VTE is fair as wording, but the interval (0.77 to 1.39) cannot exclude a moderate effect.

anchors.locator: Figure 3, peripheral artery disease and abdominal aortic aneurysm rows; Results › Associations With CVD, 1st paragraph
Figure 3, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, venous thromboembolism and aortic valve stenosis rows
Results › Associations With CVD, 1st and 3rd paragraphs
anchors.extracted: Aortic valve stenosis: suggestive positive associations in weighted median and MR-Egger; directional pleiotropy indicated only for this outcome (test not named in the text). rs1229984 alone associated (P<0.05) with PAD, AVS and AAA (supplement Table XIII).

anchors.locator: Discussion › Strengths and Limitations, 3rd paragraph; Figure 1
anchors.extracted: Low precision for outcomes with few cases; UK Biobank used in variant discovery and in exposure and most outcome datasets, which may bias estimates; HF, VTE, PAD, AVS and AAA outcome data from UK Biobank only.

key_findings.note: The main text does not name MR-Egger as the test that indicated directional pleiotropy; it is the likely one (Table X, not read).

reporting_issues.note: Found independently on the enlarged figures.

risk_of_bias.note: Some concerns overall; the domain notes match the source (smoking-linked instrument, sample overlap, no F statistic, outcome consortia partly multi-ancestry).

interpretation_gap.note: Minor; the Conclusions' causal wording for stroke and peripheral artery disease leans on MR assumptions that the smoking association strains.

missed: Discussion › Comparison With Other Studies, 1st paragraph: the paper misdescribes the studies it compares with. It reports Holmes et al. as about 10% lower coronary odds per additional alcohol-lowering allele, whereas Holmes compared carriers with non-carriers (dominant model). It gives China Kadoorie Biobank's genotyped sample as 161 490, whereas Millwood et al. report 161 498. This is a minor reporting issue; claims should take those figures from the original papers.
